_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Tuvalu covering Polynesian settlement (~3000 years ago), Ellice Islands naming (British, 1819), European contact (Alvaro de Mendaña 1568 Nui atoll), blackbirding/labour trade (1860s-70s, Peruvian slavers), Gilbert and Ellice Islands Colony (British, 1892-1975), separation from Kiribati 1975 (Ellice Islanders Polynesian voted to separate from Gilbertese Micronesian), independence 1978, .tv internet domain (major revenue), climate change existential crisis (lowest-lying nation candidate, maximum elevation 4.6m).

religion.note: Ekalesia Kelisiano Tuvalu (Church of Tuvalu, Congregational, ~92%, established by London Missionary Society, effectively state church, deeply embedded in island life); Baha'i (significant for tiny population); near-universal Christianity; church attendance near 100%; pastor (faifeau) holds major social authority; pre-Christian beliefs (Pulefolau, ancestor worship, banished by missionaries) entirely displaced; Sunday strictly observed; church donations significant portion of family income

ethnic_groups.name: Tuvaluan (Polynesian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Polynesian; closely related to Samoans/Tongans; extremely homogeneous; nine inhabited atolls (Tuvalu means 'eight standing together', originally 8 inhabited, Niulakita added); te ano (traditional ball game, entire island participates); fatele (song-dance, community performance); communal living; subsistence (fishing, coconut, pulaka/taro pit cultivation); aliki (chiefs, hereditary, village governance); some of most isolated communities on Earth

ethnic_groups.name: Gilbertese (I-Kiribati)
ethnic_groups.notes: Nui atoll (settled by Gilbertese, Micronesian language spoken); legacy of Gilbert and Ellice Islands Colony; voted to stay with Tuvalu despite ethnic ties to Kiribati

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed Polynesian/Micronesian; European (few); seasonal workers; significant diaspora (New Zealand ~3k, seafarers globally, Tuvalu Trust Fund established 1987 by UK/NZ/Australia for post-phosphate/post-climate support)

independence.from: United Kingdom (separated from Gilbert Islands 1975, became Tuvalu; Gilbert Islands became Kiribati 1979)

country_profile.notes_unique: .tv internet domain (Tuvalu's ISO code is TV, leased .tv domain to Verisign, generates ~$5-10M/year, ~10% of government revenue, ironic lifeline for sinking nation, used by Twitch.tv etc.); climate change poster child (alongside Kiribati/Marshall Islands, average elevation 2m, maximum 4.6m, saltwater intrusion destroying crops, king tides flooding regularly, PM Natano at UN 'We are sinking', Australia 2023 Falepili Union treaty offered climate refuge/residency to all Tuvaluans, first climate migration treaty, sovereignty-in-perpetuity even if islands submerge); 4th smallest country (26 km², only Vatican/Monaco/Nauru smaller); 3rd least populated (only Vatican/Nauru fewer people); Funafuti (capital atoll, ~6k people, WWII US airbase, overcrowded lagoon-side, South Pacific's most densely populated atoll); Tuvalu Trust Fund (established 1987 by UK/Australia/NZ/Japan/South Korea, endowment fund, investments, interest supplements government revenue, ~$100M, smart financial mechanism for tiny nation); blackbirding (1860s-70s, Peruvian/Fijian/Queensland labour traders kidnapped ~400 Tuvaluans as slaves, devastating for small population, some never returned); no military (police force only); seafarers (Tuvaluan men work as merchant seafarers worldwide, trained by Tuvalu Maritime Training Institute, remittances important); Taiwan recognition (one of few countries recognising Taiwan, now complicated by Australia Falepili deal); te ano (traditional game, large woven ball, competitive between island halves, festive event); philately (stamp sales historically significant revenue); remotest nation (one of most isolated countries, few flights, Funafuti airstrip doubles as sports field/gathering place when no planes)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Feleti Teo
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Elected by Parliament; former Attorney General; succeeded Natano; Falepili Union with Australia (climate migration treaty management); Taiwan recognition continued; development focus; quiet governance

head_of_state.name: King Charles III
head_of_state.title: King of Tuvalu
head_of_state.notes: Constitutional monarch; represented by Governor-General Tofiga Vaevalu Falani (since 2021); Tuvalu one of 14 Commonwealth realms; republic debate minimal

former_leaders.name: Kausea Natano
former_leaders.notes: Dramatic UN speeches ('We are sinking but so is everyone else'); Falepili Union with Australia 2023 (climate refuge treaty, historic, sovereignty preserved even if islands submerge); Taiwan recognition maintained; COVID management (virus-free until 2022)

former_leaders.name: Enele Sopoaga
former_leaders.notes: Climate champion; Paris Agreement negotiations; 'We are not drowning, we are fighting' slogan; raised Tuvalu's global profile; Taiwan ally

former_leaders.name: Toaripi Lauti
former_leaders.notes: First PM at independence; led separation from Gilbert Islands; nation builder; founding father
